newsitem.title: USA: Atlantic Tele-Network OKs split in two cos.
newsitem.headline: Atlantic Tele-Network OKs split in two cos.

text.p: Atlantic Tele-Network Inc said Tuesday its board of directors approved the split of Atlantic into two separate companies.
The company, which announced the proposed split in January, will put its U.S. Virgin Islands operations in Emerging Communications Inc and its Guyana operations into Atlantic Tele-Network.
The company said each current Atlantic stockholder will receive four-tenths of a share of new Atlantic stock and one share of Emerging stock for each current share.
The company also said it will repurchase 765,564 Atlantic shares for $17.4 million, or $22.72 a share, from co-chief executive Cornelius Prior and his trust.
Prior will own about 57 percent of the new Atlantic stock, while Atlantic's other co-chief executive, Jeffrey Prosser, will control Emerging, holding about 52 percent of its common stock.

Prudential Securities Inc said the transaction is fair to public stockholders from a financial point of view, according to Atlantic. It added Prior and Prosser, who own 60 percent of Atlantic's current stock, agreed to vote in favor of the split.

The company said the transaction is dependent on obtaining $17.4 million of long-term financing by Emerging to buy Prior's current Atlantic stock; an Internal Revenue Service ruling that the transfer of assets and liabilities to Emerging and the distribution of Emerging stock to current Atlantic stockholders will be tax free; and the listing of Emerging's stock and Atlantic's continued listing on the American Stock Exchange.
Atlantic's share traded at 13-1/4 Tuesday morning, up 1-1/8.
